purpose: Run every installable beat/downbeat/tempo/meter tracker on identical audio so a disagreement is about the music, not about resampling.

BEAT_THIS.paper: Foscarin et al., 'Beat this! Accurate beat tracking without DBN postprocessing', ISMIR 2024

MADMOM.licence: BSD-2-Clause (code), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (models and data files)
MADMOM.commercialUse: BLOCKED for the shipped models. madmom's own LICENSE splits the package: the source is BSD-2-Clause and commercially usable, but the pre-trained model files this worker loads (RNNDownBeatProcessor) are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and explicitly require written permission from Gerhard Widmer before inclusion in a commercial product. Treated here as a measurement-only contender: it may be benchmarked, and it may NOT be routed to in a shipped product without that permission.
MADMOM.paper: Böck et al., 'madmom: a new Python Audio and Music Signal Processing Library', ACM MM 2016

LIBROSA.note: Dynamic-programming beat tracker with no downbeat model at all; reports downbeats as null rather than guessing. Included as the honest floor.
LIBROSA.paper: Ellis, 'Beat Tracking by Dynamic Programming', J. New Music Research 2007

BEATNET.commercialUse: permitted for BeatNet itself, but it imports madmom at runtime and therefore inherits madmom's model restriction wherever a madmom model file is loaded.
BEATNET.paper: Heydari et al., 'BeatNet: CRNN and Particle Filtering for Online Joint Beat, Downbeat and Meter Tracking', ISMIR 2021

ALL_IN_ONE.commercialUse: permitted (Demucs weights it pulls are MIT; the htdemucs bag is CC-BY-NC for some variants — check before routing)
ALL_IN_ONE.note: Requires NATTEN, which compiles against torch. Optional layer in the image: if it is absent the worker says so instead of pretending.
ALL_IN_ONE.paper: Kim & Nam, 'All-In-One Metrical And Functional Structure Analysis With Neighborhood Attentions', WASPAA 2023

consideredAndRejected.name: skip_that_beat
consideredAndRejected.reason: Publishes a training-time augmentation for underrepresented time signatures (2/4, 3/4) and the training code, not a released inference checkpoint. Directly relevant to the odd-metre condition, but there is no model to run.

consideredAndRejected.name: BEAST
consideredAndRejected.reason: Online/streaming beat tracker. The platform's analysis path is offline, where a streaming transformer is a handicap, not an advantage.

consideredAndRejected.name: Beat Transformer
consideredAndRejected.reason: Checkpoint is distributed via a Google Drive link with no published digest; a weight we cannot verify is a weight we do not deploy.
